newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Kenwood warns on H2 profits, names CEO.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Kenwood warns on H2 profits, names CEO.

text.p: Britain's Kenwood Appliances Plc on Tuesday issued a warning on second-half profits and said it had named a new chief executive to help boost shareholder value.
The profit warning sent Kenwood shares tumbling, with the stock down by 38 pence, or 20 percent, to 148 after a hitting a low of 115.
The maker of domestic appliances said it expected pretax profits in the second half ending on April 4 to fall significantly below the first half's level.
Kenwood previously posted first-half pretax profits of 3.29 million pounds ($5.3 million) for the six months to October 4, down from 7.40 million pounds in the period a year ago.

The company said its current managing director, Tim Beech, would be leaving the company and be replaced by Colin Gordon, previously a director of the IDV wine and spirit unit at food and drinks giant Grand Metropolitan Plc.
Gordon will join the company as chief executive, with effect from March 3, following Beech's departure on February 28.

"Colin brings extensive fast-moving consumer goods and European experience to Kenwood and has valuable expertise in marketing leading international brands," Kenwood chairman David Nash said in a statement.
"I look forward to working with him to develop Kenwood and grow shareholder value," he added.
Kenwood said that although it was maintaining market share, trading conditions in western Europe remained extremely difficult, with margins continuing to come under pressure.
The company had previously said it expected to see some improvement in margins in the second half.
Kenwood also said the strength of sterling in the second half would have a significant impact on profitability since it does about three-quarters of its business outside the UK.
The company said it was still reviewing its operations and expected to provide details about possible related costs when it announced results for the year.

Last month Kenwood shareholders voted against a resolution requiring it to talk to third parties about selling the company. Kenwood confirmed it had received an approach from rival Pifco but said it had never received a formal bid. ($1=.6161 Pound)
